topics.title: Common Table Expressions (CTEs)
topics.description: Build readable multi-step queries with named intermediate results.
topics.lessonMarkdown:
## CTEs as query-building blocks

CTEs let you write a query as a sequence of named transformations.

```sql
WITH regional_sales AS (
  SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT region, revenue
FROM regional_sales
WHERE revenue > 1500;
```

For advanced tasks, think of each CTE as a small, testable intermediate result.

workedExamples.explanation: The outer query reads like a second analytical step.

workedExamples.task: Prepare a clean aggregate before applying a limit.
workedExamples.query: WITH person_sales AS (SELECT salesperson, SUM(amount) AS total_sales FROM sales GROUP BY salesperson) SELECT salesperson, total_sales FROM person_sales ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 2;

pages.title: Understand the idea
pages.content:
A Common Table Expression (CTE) gives a name to an intermediate query result for the duration of one statement. It can make multi-step analytics easier to read and reuse.

```sql
WITH regional_sales AS (
  SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY region
)
SELECT * FROM regional_sales
WHERE revenue > 1500;
```
